chunks: Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A woman performs sa‘i between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah on a riding animal or on a camel? He said: “There is no problem with that.”
He said: And I asked him about a man doing that. He said: “There is no problem with it, and walking is better.”

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two points of sa‘i in hajj and ‘umrah
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the second point between which sa‘i is performed
key_terms.تَسْعَى: performs sa‘i, moving between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah as part of the rite
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection or legal problem

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform sa‘i between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah while riding, and is walking better?
ai.summary: This hadith states that performing sa‘i between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah while riding is permissible for both women and men. At the same time, it clarifies that walking remains the more virtuous way. The narration is a jurisprudential ruling related to the rites of hajj.
